private_notes.observations: Birchwood Hale’s rate of $245 in Q3 was $4 below both competitors and received 692 hours, versus 665 hours at $249 in Q2. private_notes.plan: Set a rate just below the recent competitor level to retain a modest price advantage while recovering some margin. Compare the next allocation and rate card with prior quarters before making further moves; avoid assuming the small Q2-to-Q3 allocation change was caused solely by price.

Q3’s $249 rate was above Birchwood’s $245, so the prior strategy’s proposed $1 undercut would mean pricing at $244 this quarter. private_notes.plan: Set $244 to test whether a $1 undercut of Birchwood wins enough additional hours to offset the lower margin. Compare this quarter’s allocation and the next rate card with prior quarters before deciding whether to continue matching or undercutting.

private_notes.observations: When Birchwood Hale was above both competitors in Q4 ($248 versus $245 and $244), its allocation fell to 626 hours. private_notes.plan: Set $243 to match Birchwood. Track whether matching the lowest rate preserves allocation; avoid further undercutting unless subsequent results show it is necessary.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $243 rather than undercutting the two firms at $242. Compare next quarter’s allocation and rate card to see whether being $1 above rivals materially costs hours; adjust only if the evidence supports it.
